exposure: Teenage pregnancy before and during the COVID-19 pandemic
Deliveries between 2017-2019 (control group) vs. deliveries between 2020-2022 (study group)
outcome: Maternal outcomes (cesarean delivery rate, preference for long-acting reversible contraception (LARC) methods)
Neonatal outcomes (low birth weight (LBW), stillbirth rate)
cohort: 1210 teenage pregnancies delivered between January 2017 and December 2022 at Nakhon Nayok General Hospital in Thailand
finding: The rate of preterm births among teenage pregnancies decreased during the COVID-19 pandemic, and there was an increase in the preference for LARC methods among teenage pregnancy cases.
